A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UrbanCAD and contain the main paper and supplementary Sections 7–11. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original vehicle-rendering experiments, simulated perception evaluations, and material and lighting comparisons, including Tables 1–5.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds geometry measurements on 30 ShapeNet vehicles and qualitative recovery examples from partial observations.

M1.justification: The retrieval, material assignment, optimization losses, and lighting/compositing pipeline are retained. V2 clarifies albedo-only optimization; v1 already fixed roughness parameters and described assigning glass materials directly. These clarifications do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds direct geometry evaluation using ShapeNet vehicles in Section 10.4 and recovery from occluded input images in Figure 6. ShapeNet previously supplied baseline pretraining data, while occlusion scenarios concerned downstream perception. KITTI-360 and MVMC coverage remains.

E2.justification: Matched photorealism, perception, lighting, and MVMC experiments retain their comparison methods. The added geometry benchmark reuses Wonder3D, already evaluated in v1, rather than introducing or modifying a competing algorithm.

E3.justification: The new geometry evaluation randomly selects 30 ShapeNet vehicles, retrieves corresponding Objaverse models, and measures Chamfer distance and volume IoU. Existing rendering and perception evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds four qualitative examples testing vehicle recovery from partial observations. Existing material and lighting ablations, perception analyses, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added geometry results also use point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports UrbanCAD/Wonder3D Chamfer distances of 0.052/0.058 and volume IoU of 0.636/0.588. Figure 6 adds recovery results, and several Figure 5 renderings change. Numerical results in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The retrieval formulation, rendering equations, and loss definitions in Equations 1–9 retain their mathematical content. The new geometry metrics are named without introducing formal definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions, and conclusion retain the claims of single-image construction of photorealistic, controllable vehicles, realistic scene insertion, and usefulness for challenging perception evaluations. Revised emphasis on expert-designed priors does not change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking occlusion resilience to SAM training, semantic retrieval, and part-aware losses. Section 10.4 attributes better geometry scores to unobserved-region quality. Existing geometry mismatches, lighting limitations, and failure conditions remain documented.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly identifies metal/rubber albedo as optimized and glass as assigned without optimization. It notes automatic GroundedSAM segmentation and annotation or trajectory sources for insertion positions. Section 7.5 reframes manual material-prior selection as a recommendation.

R1.justification: V2 adds the survey Recent Advances in Implicit Representation-Based 3D Shape Generation and CAT, and removes Mask2CAD. The introductory PhotoScene comparison is shortened, while the broader positioning against reconstruction and material-transfer approaches remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are locally rewritten to emphasize geometry and material priors and streamline the motivation. Method explanations are clarified and experimental discussions added, while the overall section organization is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 6 and Table 6, adds a GT column to Figure 4, updates several Figure 5 renderings, and moves Table 1 from page 7 to page 6. Existing appendix figures are retained with shifted numbering; the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Table 6 supplies direct quantitative geometry evidence missing from v1, while Figure 6 adds occlusion examples and Section 3.3 clarifies what is optimized. These additions modestly strengthen validation and clarity. The geometry evaluation is small and briefly specified, and the occlusion evidence is qualitative, so the overall improvement is limited.
